messages:
dmitri: Heads-up — seeing a small cluster of NVIDIA Xid 79 events in us-west-2-gpupool-3 starting ~01:04 UTC. ECC correctable counts nudged up on 3 different nodes. Posting raw observations + quick triage thread.

maya: which workloads were active on those nodes? any long-form decode or heavy KV-cache churn?

infra-bot: gpu-uw2-23: Xid 79 @ 01:05:12, PCI 0000:3b:00.0, ecc_correctable=2, ecc_uncorrectable=0
gpu-uw2-41: Xid 79 @ 01:06:03, ecc_correctable=1
gpu-uw2-23: Xid 13 @ 01:07:45 (single event)

maya: thanks — looks like 79 is the common one. On the cluster history those GPUs were running a mix: two streaming chat workers (redwood-opt-13b streaming) + one long-run embedding batch.

ops-oncall: I'm on it. Draining gpu-uw2-23 now and tagging it flaky-xid79. Will reschedule pods to spare nodes and avoid allocs for heavy decode jobs.

alex: re: scheduling — pushed a temporary placement rule to avoid placing streaming-decoder tasks on any node with tag flaky-xid79 or with last_xid_ts < 24h. Also bumped QA pool capacity by +2 to absorb.

sarah: ran a quick correlation across the last 72h: 92 Xid 79 events total across us-west-2. 79% coincide with seq_len > 1024 and continuous decode (no batching). Embedding-only jobs show <5% of Xid79 overlap.

maya: that matches my hypothesis — KV cache churn + long sequences seem correlated. Any telemetry on per-token mem pressure?

infra-bot: sample nvml summary (gpu-uw2-23): 
```
GPU 0: redwood-opt-13b (streaming) — memory occupied 32.7GB / 48GB, pstate P0, encoder threads active, sm utilization 92%
ECC correctable events: 2 (last 24h)
Xid events: [79 @ 01:05:12, 13 @ 01:07:45]
```

dmitri: good catch. Two follow-ups: 1) can we add short-circuit limits on continuous-decoder workers (max_decode_steps=1024) as a safety net? 2) schedule deeper hardware diagnostics / vendor memtests on nodes with >=2 Xid79 in 24h.

ops-oncall: implemented (1) — max_decode_steps enforcement rolled to us-west-2 streaming autoscaling group via feature-flag for next 6h. Also kicked off vendor memtest for gpu-uw2-23 and gpu-uw2-41 (job id job-4872).

alex: created an anomaly alert rule: if a node gets >=2 Xid79 within 6h, auto-tag and prevent streaming-decoder scheduling and spin up replacement from reserve. Also added a dashboard panel that correlates Xid counts with seq_len distribution and model type.

sarah: side note — Xid 13 spikes appear unrelated (single events, coincident with preemption/driver reload). No widespread 13 trend. Xid 79 seems hardware-flaky under sustained decode workloads.

maya: any cost implications? if we divert streaming to other regions we might pay cross-region egress or use hotter nodes.

dmitri: short term cost hit is acceptable vs risk. Long term we should consider model-splitting: host long-context streaming on Dedicated pools with newer cards (A10->A100 transition) and keep embeddings on cheaper quantized instances.

ops-oncall: update — gpu-uw2-23 memtest returned with ECC parity passes but vendor recommends running extended burn (24h). I left node drained and flagged for replacement if another Xid79 occurs.

dmitri: action items: 
- ops-oncall: keep node drained until memtest complete and vendor RMA decided (due in 24-48h).
- alex: keep the auto-tag + scheduler rule active for 72h and capture traces.
- sarah: produce a short report (CSV) correlating Xid79 with model, seq_len, and container image (due EOD).
- maya: propagate temporary limits to streaming workers in prod and staging.

maya: acked, will update the runbook with Xid79 cohort steps (drain->memtest->RMA threshold: >=2 in 24h).

dmitri: thanks all. If anyone sees Xid48/31/79 clusters pop up in other regions, ping this thread. For now marking this incident as monitoring/triage. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-uw2-xid79-cohort, linked job-4872.

ops-oncall: closing the immediate triage loop — will post final RMA decision in this thread.
